newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Doubt cast on size of Indonesian gold find.
newsitem.headline: Doubt cast on size of Indonesian gold find.

text.p: The U.S. and Indonesian partners of a Canadian mining company in what had been billed as the gold find of the century said on Thursday their participation depended on whether the project was economically feasible.

Canadian exploration company Bre-X Minerals Ltd said in a statement from Canada on Wednesday there appeared to be a "strong possibility" that the potential gold resources on the Busang property in Indonesia's East Kalimantan province had been overstated.

On February 17, Bre-X had issued a statement estimating gold reserves at Busang at 70.95 million ounces, making it the biggest discovery since gold was struck on South Africa's Witwatersrand late last century.

The U.S. mining company Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc, which was to develop Busang, said in a statement on Wednesday that analyses of its own drilling results so far "indicate insignificant amounts of gold".
A spokeswoman for Indonesia's Nusamba group said on Thursday the Indonesian and U.S. partners would develop Busang, in the rain forests of Borneo island, only if it was economically feasible.

"Nusamba, Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc and its Indonesian partners would like to participate in the development of the Busang project only if development is economically feasible," Nia Sarinastiti of public relations company PT Mekurindo, which represents the proposed Busang joint venture company, told Reuters.
Freeport is currently conducting a highly detailed survey of the Busang site.
Wednesday's Bre-X announcement caused pandemonium on the Toronto Stock Exchange, which suspended trading in Bre-X shares.

Bre-X shares had been hit late last week following the death of the company's chief geologist, Filipino Michael de Guzman, and an Indonesian newspaper report questioning the size of the Busang reserves. An Indonesian airport official said de Guzman may have committed suicide.
